title: Reel — a clock, a gate and a handful of chance

steps.note: A complex oscillator, a quad low pass gate, a clock and a random generator. Four modules, and nothing patched between them yet.
The oscillator runs continuously. The gate decides when any of it is heard.
Nothing yet. The gate is shut, and a shut gate is silence rather than a quiet sound.
The clock's first output strikes the gate. Each strike opens it and lets it fall closed again.
And there it is — a pluck, because that is what a gate does to a drone.
The tempo is not a knob. It is a window, and clicking it opens every value it can take.
Each of the three clocks holds a ratio to the master. This one now runs at twice the tempo.
Swing drags every second pulse late, and the pair still takes the time two straight ones would.
The master clock now drives a random generator — Émilie Gillet's Marbles, ported here from her own source.
Its first voltage output goes to the oscillator's pitch. The rhythm is the clock's; the notes are chance.
Steps quantises those voltages. Turned up it narrows the scale rather than switching it, until only the root is left.
Déjà vu is the loop. Set a length, turn the knob up, and the random becomes a phrase that comes round again.
Four notes, chosen by chance and then kept.
Back to the middle and it forgets again.
And that is four modules, six cables, and about a minute.
